clue.text: Slight alteration in a jacket people sport during American races

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket

indicators.note: during says the people come in the middle of the races, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TT stands for Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races
men means people in the general sense

explanation.surface: A spectator tweaks the formal jacket worn to the races in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' only links: it is what people do with a jacket. 'during' places the people within the races; the Isle of Man TT is a motorcycle event.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tweak or modification is a minor change made to correct or improve something.

clue.text: Old opponent on adventure? No way

parts.note: someone anti is against, an opponent

indicators.note: No says the way is to be taken out of the adventure

parts.note: a quest is an adventurous journey
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An old rival is asked to join an expedition and refuses flatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like a refusal; 'No' removes ST from QUEST to leave QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antique dates from long ago, so it is old in the sense of vintage or ancient.

clue.text: Pickle and aromatic leaf the French put in a Cajun dish

parts.note: a jam is a fix or pickle, a tight spot

indicators.note: put in tells us the French article goes inside the leaf

parts.note: bay leaves are aromatic and used in cooking
la is French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A recipe: pickle and bay leaf with a French touch go into a Louisiana dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' reads as a condiment but means a predicament, JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Louisiana rice dish with meat or seafood, a classic of Cajun cooking.

clue.text: Begin with tiniest portion of steak pie

indicators.note: the tiniest portion of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a tart is a pastry pie

explanation.surface: Advice to start eating with just a morsel of steak pie.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to commence or begin it; both are verbs of setting off.

clue.text: Code-breaker's mother becoming wiser

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Alan Turing was the famous Bletchley Park code-breaker of the Second World War

explanation.surface: The code-breaker's mum is growing wiser with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older and wiser is developing into adulthood, coming of age in judgment as well as years.

clue.text: Present one's excuses, to begin with? Absolutely not

parts.note: now is the present time
one's read as one is, I plus IS

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of excuses

explanation.surface: Should one apologise straight away? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb (offer excuses) but is the noun, NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in no way at all, an emphatic negative.

clue.text: Soft wet earth churned around ditch

indicators.note: churned around says the wet earth is turned the other way round

parts.note: mud is wet earth
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Soft muddy ground gets churned up round a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like part of the landscape but is the verb, to discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of or discard it, as you would at a tip.

clue.text: Political extremist showing some youthful traits

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political firebrand still shows some traits of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra holds extreme views, especially in politics; the word is used as a noun for a hardliner.

clue.text: Pastor placed over Spanish region for example

indicators.note: in a down answer, placed over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A clergyman posted to a Spanish region, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example for others to follow.

clue.text: Fervent macho types held in check

indicators.note: held in puts the macho types inside the check

parts.note: to vet is to check or screen
he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: Passionate tough guys are being kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe strong, passionate feeling expressed forcefully.

clue.text: US city circulated some cheap material

indicators.note: circulated tells us that run is read backwards
some says a run of letters is taken from inside cheap material

explanation.surface: An American city has been distributing cheap fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Possibly keep various members of sect inside Northants town

indicators.note: inside puts those rearranged letters within the tower

parts.note: a keep is a castle's tower, so a tower is possibly a keep

indicators.note: various members of says the letters of sect are rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of a religious sect might hold out in a castle keep in a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various members of' signals the rearrangement and 'inside' the insertion. Northants is short for Northamptonshire, an English county; 'Possibly' flags the keep as an example of a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a market town in Northamptonshire, known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Only a few ounces? Pity

definitions.meaning: a ... of a pound is four ounces, only a few
to give no mercy, as in 'no ... given', means to show no pity

explanation.surface: Someone laments a tiny portion: what a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British weights: a pound is sixteen ounces, so a quarter-pound is four.
explanation.definitionFit: Four ounces are a quarter of a pound; quarter also means clemency shown to a beaten enemy.

clue.text: Girl's report on the situation

parts.note: a girl is a she; the possessive gives no letters
a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: A young woman's briefing on the state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like an account but is the noise of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means an affair or matter, as in 'the whole' state of things.

clue.text: Tough working in adult-rated movies, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: X was the old British certificate for adult films, so performing in them is X acting

explanation.surface: Appearing in adult films is hard work, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding task is tough, making great demands on skill or effort.

clue.text: Meal making you remarkably awake, passing through loch

indicators.note: passing through puts the rearranged letters inside the loch

parts.note: Loch Tay is a Scottish loch

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of awake are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A meal that keeps you wide awake while crossing a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' signals the rearrangement and 'passing through' places it within the loch; 'making you' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bought-in hot meal eaten at home is a takeout, which Britons call by this name.

clue.text: Reduce length of class given by lecturer

indicators.note: given by lecturer suggests words spoken out loud to a hall

parts.note: a lesson is a class period, a length of time spent in class

explanation.surface: A lecturer cuts the length of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to reduce it or make it smaller.

clue.text: One leaving team trials in disarray suspected something amiss

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of team trials, less the one leaving, are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: When a player walked out of chaotic team trials, someone sensed trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' says I is taken out of TEAM TRIALS; the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that something is wrong, like a dog sniffing out vermin.

clue.text: At least four teams going north round extremely twisty US route

indicators.note: round puts the reversed teams around the end letters
in a down answer, going north means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a team is an XI, eleven players; XIS twice is two lots of teams, so at least four

indicators.note: extremely picks the two end letters of twisty

explanation.surface: A convoy of teams heads north on a winding American road.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team is an XI, so plural teams are XIS; two lots make at least four. 'going north' reverses them, 'extremely' takes the ends of twisty, and 'round' encloses those.
explanation.definitionFit: Route 66 is the historic US highway from Chicago to Santa Monica.

clue.text: Funny business admitted by this French politician

indicators.note: admitted by puts the funny business inside the French word

parts.note: ce is French for this
a lark is a bit of fun, a prank

explanation.surface: A French politician confesses to some monkey business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this French' is not a French politician: Kenneth Clarke was a long-serving British Conservative minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Clarke was a senior British Conservative minister and Chancellor of the Exchequer.

clue.text: Edward Woodward ultimately tucked into fish and cheese

indicators.note: tucked into puts the pieces inside the fish

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Woodward

explanation.surface: The actor Edward Woodward finally tucks into a fish and cheese supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese named after a village in Somerset.

clue.text: Film about retreating soldiers getting abuse

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: retreating says the soldiers are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A war film about troops in retreat attracts abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie but is a thin layer, MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat someone is to abuse them; both are verbs of cruel handling.

clue.text: Line in sort of artier short film

indicators.note: in puts the line inside the rearranged letters
sort of signals that artier is rearranged into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A line of dialogue in a rather arty short film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ARTIER to TRAIER, and L goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema preview of a forthcoming movie is a short promotional film.

clue.text: To behave amorously is low in school

indicators.note: in puts the low inside the school

parts.note: to low is to moo, the cow's call

explanation.surface: Canoodling is frowned upon at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective (frowned on) but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle is to behave amorously, an informal word for necking.

clue.text: Declare divorcée's intention to save hundred pounds

indicators.note: to save says the hundred pounds are held within

parts.note: a divorcée is an ex; the possessive gives no letters
an aim is an intention
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: A divorcée announces her plan to put away a hundred pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out or proclaim something is to declare it loudly.

clue.text: In slow-moving vehicle husband's kept map out

indicators.note: kept says the husband is held within the vehicle

parts.note: a cart is a slow-moving horse-drawn vehicle
H is the abbreviation for husband; the possessive gives no letters

explanation.surface: A husband stuck in a slow vehicle has his route planned out.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart a course is to plan or plot it, as on a map.

clue.text: Illicit drug, one which is not quite enough for woman

parts.note: a tab is a tablet of an illicit drug such as LSD
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not quite enough says the word falls short of its last letter

parts.note: that can stand for which, as in 'the one that I saw'

explanation.surface: One dose of an illegal drug isn't enough for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a woman's given name, from the Aramaic for gazelle.

clue.text: Might this cause controversial UK bar?

definitions.text: Might this cause controversial UK bar?

indicators.note: controversial suggests stirring up the letters of UK bar into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Would this garment provoke a contentious ban in Britain?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the garment could indeed prompt a controversial ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-body covering worn by some Muslim women, the subject of debates over banning.

clue.text: Turning tail, son thus hurried to get help for singer

indicators.note: Turning tail says the whole string of pieces is read from the end backwards

parts.note: so means thus
ran means hurried
aid means help

explanation.surface: A son flees in a hurry to fetch help for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' reads like running away; it reverses SSORANAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana Ross is the American singer who led the Supremes.

clue.text: Hotel not in industrial area by a lake, in the country

indicators.note: not in says the hotel is removed from the industrial area

parts.note: the Ruhr is Germany's industrial heartland
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: No hotel in a factory district beside a lake out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Regular appearances of artist unknown in smart hotel

indicators.note: regular appearances of picks every other letter of artist

parts.note: z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A painter is often seen at a posh hotel, with no one knowing who he is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz in London is a famously luxurious hotel, a byword for glamour.

clue.text: Spellbinding person following performer after start of this talent show

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind that opening letter
start of points to the opening letter of this

parts.note: a hex is a spell, binding someone by magic
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A spellbinding singer follows another act on a TV talent contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spellbinding person' reads as one idea; split it: HEX is the spell, and 'person' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British TV singing contest judged by Simon Cowell, a well-known talent competition.
